---
title: Holds and retries
description: Keep one process of a connector writing at a time, keep its place between runs, send a failed request again without harm, and report each run.
---

A connector can be started twice by mistake, lose the network mid-write, or crash between two requests.

## With the kit

[The connector kit](/build/connector) handles all three, so a connector built on it needs nothing from this page. It takes the hold under a name of its own and renews it, keeps the state document with `state.get` and `state.set`, saving it only when every write in the run landed, and reports each run. On a schedule, it waits out an instance that is busy or out of reach, at least as long as `Retry-After` asks, and tries again. The [kit's README](https://github.com/withmarfa/plugins/blob/main/template/README.md#run-it) says how to run it.

## On the API

The sections below are the operations underneath, for a connector built directly on the API. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a [TypeScript SDK](/reference/typescript-sdk) client made with the connector's key, and `connectorId` is the registration's ID.

### Order a run

This order survives a stop at any step:

1. [Take the hold](#take-the-hold), and renew it for as long as the run lasts.
2. Read the [state document](#keep-your-place) and the [agreements](/build/connector-push#watch-for-changes-made-in-marfa) you need.
3. Read the vendor, and write the items.
4. Write the agreements for what you wrote or carried.
5. Replace the state document with the new place.
6. [Report the run](#report-a-run), then release the hold.

### Take the hold

The hold lets **one process at a time** write the connector's state document and agreements. Before it writes either, a process [takes the hold](/reference/api/connector-state/takeConnectorHold) under a name of its own, such as a UUID made when it starts. Two processes that share a name look like one to Marfa.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/hold
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "process": "8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9c1b-5b3e1c3e0a2d" }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const processName = crypto.randomUUID();

await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/hold", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { process: processName },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{ "expires_at": "2026-11-19T00:26:41.000Z", "ttl_seconds": 180, "renewed": false }
```

The hold lasts `ttl_seconds` from each take or renewal. While another process holds it, Marfa refuses the take, and `details.expires_at` says when that hold ends:

```json title="Response" status="409"
{
  "error": {
    "code": "connector_held",
    "message": "Another process holds this connector, or this one does not.",
    "details": { "expires_at": "2026-11-19T00:26:41.000Z" }
  }
}
```

Once a hold lapses, any process can take it.

#### Renew it while the process runs

Send the same request, under the same name, **well before `expires_at`**. The kit renews every third of `ttl_seconds`; time renewals from that, not by comparing clocks.

- **`renewed: true`** means your hold was live, so no other process wrote.
- **`renewed: false`** is expected on the first take. On a renewal, it means your hold [lapsed](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md#connectorshold-lapsed-not-renewed), and another process may have written: **read the state and agreements again** before you write.

If a renewal doesn't land, you can't know whether the hold is still yours once `expires_at` passes. **Stop writing**, to Marfa and to the vendor, until a renewal succeeds: Marfa can't stop you changing the vendor.

When the process ends cleanly, [release the hold](/reference/api/connector-state/releaseConnectorHold), so the next process can start at once. Marfa answers `{ "ok": true }` whether or not this process held it, and never releases another's:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
DELETE /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/hold?process=8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9c1b-5b3e1c3e0a2d
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.DELETE("/connectors/{id}/hold", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId }, query: { process: processName } },
});
```

A [heartbeat](/reference/api/connectors/sendConnectorHeartbeat) says the connector is alive. It neither takes nor renews the hold, so send it on its own timer. Only the key the connector is registered under may send it, and any other key is refused `403 forbidden`.

### Keep your place

The state document keeps a connector's place at the vendor, such as a sync token, so a restart, even on another computer, resumes instead of reading everything again. [Get the connector's state](/reference/api/connector-state/getConnectorState) on start, and [replace it](/reference/api/connector-state/replaceConnectorState) under the hold:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
PUT /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/state
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{ "process": "8f14e45f-ceea-467a-9c1b-5b3e1c3e0a2d", "state": { "sync_token": "abc123" } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.PUT("/connectors/{id}/state", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: { process: processName, state: { sync_token: "abc123" } },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{ "problems": {}, "state": { "sync_token": "abc123" }, "updated_at": "2026-11-19T00:24:02.000Z" }
```

- **The request replaces the whole document,** up to 512 KiB. To change one value, read it, change it, and send it all.
- **Save the state last,** after everything it covers has landed. A run that stops before the save leaves the old place, and the next run writes that part again, which the natural key makes harmless.
- **`problems`** is a map of keys of your choosing to messages about work still unresolved. Apps show it on the registration; they never see the state. Send it to replace the map, leave it out to keep it, or send `{}` to clear it. Nothing else clears it, not even a run that succeeds.
- **The document belongs to the key's source,** so a new key under the same source carries on from it. If the owner [deletes it](/reference/api/connector-state/deleteConnectorState), its agreements and problems go too, and the connector reads the vendor whole.

An agreement write follows the same hold, and takes at most 500 `set` and 500 `clear` entries, with a record of at most 16 KiB each. An item ID that no item has, or whose type the key can't read, comes back in `skipped`, and the rest goes through.

### Send a request again

| Answer | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `409 connector_held` | Another process holds the hold, or this one holds none. Nothing was written. | Take the hold, after `details.expires_at` if there is one. If `renewed` is `false`, read again before you write. |
| `429 rate_limited` | The key sent too many requests. | Wait the seconds `Retry-After` names, also in `error.details.retry_after_seconds`, and send the same request. |
| `503 write_contention` | The database was busy. Nothing changed. | Send the same request again. |
| `500 internal_error` | The request may or may not have completed. | Read what you changed before you send a write again. |

A write whose answer you never saw is the hard case:

- **The state document and agreements replace what's there,** so sending one again under the hold leaves the same result.
- **A bulk write by natural key** lands on the same items. A record that changes nothing is `skipped` as `unchanged`, with no new version.
- **A write without a natural key** can make a second item, unless it carries an `Idempotency-Key`. Marfa then answers a repeat with the first answer, with `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, and writes nothing.

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: 6f1c2b8e-3d4a-4f7b-9a2e-1c5d8e7f9b30

{ "type": "shop.order", "tier": "feed", "properties": { "title": "Oil paints" } }
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/items", {
  params: { header: { "Idempotency-Key": "6f1c2b8e-3d4a-4f7b-9a2e-1c5d8e7f9b30" } },
  body: { type: "shop.order", tier: "feed", properties: { title: "Oil paints" } },
});
```

A write to the vendor is **yours to make safe**: send the vendor an idempotency key made from something that doesn't change between attempts, such as the item's ID. [Write safely](/build/write-safely) covers versions and idempotency keys in full.

### Report a run

[Report each run](/reference/api/connectors/reportConnectorRun) when it ends, with the outcome `succeeded` or `failed`:

```http tab="HTTP" tab-group="client"
POST /connectors/01a12313-d219-7e92-8869-1f6546b43dbc/runs
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "outcome": "failed",
  "started_at": "2026-11-19T09:00:00Z",
  "finished_at": "2026-11-19T09:00:04Z",
  "error": "the shop answered 503"
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
await marfa.POST("/connectors/{id}/runs", {
  params: { path: { id: connectorId } },
  body: {
    outcome: "failed",
    started_at: "2026-11-19T09:00:00Z",
    finished_at: "2026-11-19T09:00:04Z",
    error: "the shop answered 503",
  },
});
```

Reporting needs no hold, and only the connector's own key may report. The next run starts from the last state saved. The registration keeps the last 100 runs, which `marfa connectors runs <connector-id>` lists, newest first.

The rules behind this page are in the [connectors](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/connectors.md) chapter of the contract.
